_note: Plain-language summaries of laws and rules that give citizens leverage. Not legal advice; the agent must cite only provisions listed here.

provisions.title: Right to Information Act, 2005
provisions.summary: Any citizen can ask any public authority for information held by it. Reasons for asking need not be given.
key_points: Sec. 6(1): apply in writing or electronically to the Public Information Officer (PIO) of the public authority, in English, Hindi or the official language of the area.
Sec. 6(2): the applicant need not give any reason for requesting information.
Sec. 6(3): if the information is with another authority, the PIO must transfer the application within 5 days.
Sec. 7(1): information must be supplied within 30 days; within 48 hours if it concerns the life or liberty of a person.
Sec. 7(6): if the PIO misses the time limit, the information must be provided free of charge.
Sec. 19(1): first appeal to the First Appellate Authority within 30 days of the reply or of the deadline expiring.
Sec. 19(3): second appeal to the Central/State Information Commission within 90 days of the first appeal decision.
Sec. 20: the Information Commission can impose a penalty on a PIO (₹250 per day, up to ₹25,000) for delay or refusal without reasonable cause.
RTI gives access to records, file notings, status and documents — it does not compel the authority to answer 'why' questions or give opinions. Ask for records instead.

provisions.title: Right to Information Rules, 2012 (Central public authorities)
provisions.summary: Procedure for RTI applications to Central Government public authorities. States have their own rules (fees and word limits differ).
key_points: Application fee ₹10 (demand draft, banker's cheque, Indian Postal Order, or online at rtionline.gov.in for central authorities).
Applicants below the poverty line pay no fee (attach a copy of the BPL certificate).
An application should ordinarily not exceed 500 words, excluding the address of the PIO and the applicant.
Photocopies cost ₹2 per page under the central rules.

provisions.title: State Right to Public Services Acts (e.g. Assam RTPS Act, 2012)
provisions.summary: Many states guarantee delivery of notified public services within fixed time limits and allow appeals when officers miss them.
key_points: Each notified service has a designated officer and a stipulated time limit.
If the time limit lapses or the application is rejected, the citizen can appeal to the Appellate Authority.
Penalties can be imposed on officers who fail to deliver services without sufficient reason.

provisions.title: Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 — Section 198A (inserted in 2019)
provisions.summary: Makes the designated authority, contractor, consultant or concessionaire responsible for road design, construction and maintenance standards.
key_points: If failure to follow road design, construction or maintenance standards leads to death or disability, the responsible authority/contractor is punishable with a fine of up to ₹1 lakh.
Useful to cite when a reported pothole or road defect remains unrepaired and poses a safety risk.

provisions.title: Consumer Protection Act, 2019
provisions.summary: Protects consumers against defective goods, deficient services and unfair trade practices.
key_points: Complaints can be filed online through e-Daakhil; a lawyer is not mandatory.
District Commission: claims up to ₹50 lakh; State Commission: ₹50 lakh–₹2 crore; National Commission: above ₹2 crore.
Sec. 69: complaint must ordinarily be filed within 2 years from the date the cause of action arose.
Consumers can seek refund, replacement, compensation for loss or injury, and litigation costs.

provisions.title: Electricity (Rights of Consumers) Rules, 2020
provisions.summary: Gives electricity consumers enforceable rights to reliable supply, timely connections, correct billing and compensation.
key_points: New connection timelines: 7 days in metro cities, 15 days in other municipal areas, 30 days in rural areas (or as notified by the state commission, if lower).
Consumers are entitled to compensation when the DISCOM fails to meet notified standards of performance.
Every DISCOM must have a Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum; further appeal lies to the Electricity Ombudsman.

provisions.title: Reserve Bank – Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2021
provisions.summary: Free, online redress for deficiency in service by RBI-regulated entities.
key_points: First complain to the regulated entity (bank/NBFC/payment app).
If the complaint is rejected, not resolved satisfactorily, or not answered within 30 days, file at cms.rbi.org.in.
File with the Ombudsman generally within one year of receiving the entity's reply (or of the 30 days expiring).
No fee is charged.

provisions.title: National Food Security Act, 2013
provisions.summary: Legal entitlement to subsidised foodgrains for eligible households through the Public Distribution System.
key_points: Priority households are entitled to 5 kg foodgrains per person per month; Antyodaya (AAY) households to 35 kg per household per month.
Under the PM Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana, NFSA foodgrains are currently provided free of cost.
Sec. 15: every district must have a District Grievance Redressal Officer; Sec. 16: State Food Commission hears appeals.
Sec. 8: food security allowance is payable if entitled foodgrains are not supplied.

provisions.title: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005
provisions.summary: Guarantees 100 days of wage employment per year to every rural household that demands work.
key_points: Work must be provided within 15 days of a written demand; otherwise an unemployment allowance is payable.
Wages must be paid within 15 days of the closure of the muster roll; delay compensation is 0.05% of unpaid wages per day of delay.
Always ask for a dated receipt when demanding work.

provisions.title: Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009
provisions.summary: Free and compulsory education for children aged 6–14.
key_points: Sec. 12(1)(c): private unaided schools must reserve 25% of entry-level seats for children from weaker sections and disadvantaged groups.
Sec. 13: no capitation fee and no screening procedure for admission.
Complaints go to the local authority; the State Commission for Protection of Child Rights monitors RTE.

provisions.title: Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007
provisions.summary: Parents and senior citizens who cannot maintain themselves can claim maintenance from children/relatives through a Maintenance Tribunal.
key_points: Application to the Maintenance Tribunal of the sub-division; maximum maintenance up to ₹10,000 per month under the original Act (states may differ).
Tribunal should ordinarily dispose of the application within 90 days.

provisions.title: Comprehensive Guidelines for Handling Public Grievances (DARPG, 2024)
provisions.summary: Central government standards for grievance redressal on CPGRAMS.
key_points: Maximum time for redressal reduced to 21 days; an interim reply with reasons is expected if more time is needed.
Citizens can appeal on the portal if dissatisfied with the resolution.

provisions.title: Cyber fraud reporting (I4C / RBI customer liability norms)
provisions.summary: Speed matters: reporting quickly limits your liability and helps freeze money.
key_points: Call 1930 and file at cybercrime.gov.in immediately; money can often be put on hold if reported fast.

RBI's customer liability circular (2017): zero liability if an unauthorised electronic transaction caused by a third-party breach is reported within 3 working days; limited liability if reported within 4–7 working days.
Inform your bank in writing and keep the acknowledgement.
